verdict.rationale: Context.dev's timeouts documentation lets a developer set an API deadline and choose how unfinished work is handled. Its `return-partial` mode returns usable completed work with a completion marker, which trades completeness for latency at a developer-chosen cutoff. The choice between a one-response sync crawl and a background async batch adds a further latency-versus-scale choice. Missing for 10: full documentation of every unfinished-work mode beyond `return-partial` and how the deadline parameter behaves per endpoint, plus independent or hands-on corroboration that partial returns work as claimed.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trade off latency against completeness by controlling exactly when content is returned

citations.quote: Set an API deadline, choose how to handle unfinished work, and preserve partial-result markers.
`return-partial` | Return usable completed work with a completion marker. If no usable result exists, fail without a charge.
Crawl a small website section and return page Markdown in one response, with a maximum of 500 pages.
Crawl up to 25,000 pages in a background batch, track progress, and retrieve Markdown or HTML when the job finishes.
